observations: Photo 0: Dirty metal transmission casing with attached hoses, electrical connectors, and a cylindrical component on the left side; blue paint mark on the right side.
Photo 1: Side view showing a wiring harness with blue, green, and yellow wires, sensors, and an oily casing.
Photo 2: Bell housing with a circular bolt pattern and central opening where a torque converter mounts; no torque converter installed.

claims.claim: Seller is a dealer in Japanese parts and gearbox, implying this is a Japanese gearbox.
claims.evidence: No readable brand, model, or origin plate is visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Transmission may not function internally; operation cannot be confirmed from still photos.
risks.proof: Video of a bench test or shift-solenoid operation.

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage is invisible from the outside.
risks.proof: Photo of drained fluid on a magnet or borescope video of the internals.

risks.risk: Components such as the torque converter or valve body may be missing.
risks.proof: Photo showing all openings and exactly what parts are included.
Clear photo of any identification plate or sticker on the casing.

proof_requests: Clear photo of any identification plate or sticker on the transmission casing.
Video showing the transmission being bench-tested or shifted through gears.
Photo of the bell housing opening and all ports to confirm completeness.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a car gearbox from the bell housing and casing shape, so it can be priced at its worst case as non-working despite the unverified origin claim.
